title: Both legs averaged similar peak force on a single-leg hop. Which athlete showed the biggest performance drop across three hops?
explanation: B fell from 100 to 70 cm. The repeated trials reveal a drop that a single best effort misses.

title: A runner’s knee pain appears only on downhill sections. Which comparison best tests whether slope is the trigger?
options: Compare two different shoes on different hills
Repeat the same pace and distance on flat and downhill routes
Compare a sprint with a slow downhill walk
Change pace, surface and slope together
explanation: Changing one main variable makes it easier to interpret the response.

title: A climber struggles to pinch a key and compensate by bending the tip of the thumb. Which nerve supplies the muscle typically weak in this sign?
explanation: This resembles Froment’s sign. Ulnar-innervated adductor pollicis is weak and flexor pollicis longus compensates.

title: An athlete does 3 sets of 8 squats at 40 kg. Which change increases total external load by exactly 25% if everything else stays fixed?
explanation: The starting volume is 960 kg. Thirty repetitions at 40 kg gives 1,200 kg, a 25% increase.

title: Two athletes report the same pain score. Which extra detail best helps you compare how sensitive their symptoms are to activity?
options: How much activity triggers symptoms and how long they take to settle
explanation: The load needed to provoke symptoms and the recovery time describe irritability more usefully than a single score.

title: A player can push down strongly through the foot, but repeatedly catches their toes when walking. Which action is most directly limited?
explanation: Dorsiflexion lifts the front of the foot so the toes clear the ground during swing.

title: Scrub through a step-down. During which frame is the knee farthest forward relative to the planted ankle?
explanation: At the tap, the knee is farthest forward of the planted ankle. The exercise can look very different at different points in the repetition.

title: A student raises their straight leg. They feel a familiar pull that changes when their ankle moves while the hip stays still. What is the most defensible conclusion?
options: The response may involve neural sensitivity and needs context
The ankle is the source of all symptoms
explanation: Changing a distant joint can alter neural loading, but the response alone cannot establish a diagnosis.

title: A lifter’s shoulder blade lifts away from the rib cage during a wall push. Which muscle normally helps keep it against the chest wall?
explanation: Serratus anterior protracts and helps hold the scapula against the thorax.
hint: Its nerve is the long thoracic nerve.

title: A patient’s best knee flexion measures 115° today and 118° next time. Your procedure can vary by about 5°. What should you conclude?
options: The second measurement must be wrong
The change alone is too small to separate from measurement variation
explanation: An apparent change smaller than the expected variation should be interpreted cautiously.

title: An athlete completes a side plank for 60 seconds on the right and 45 on the left. What percentage of the right-side time is the left-side time?
explanation: 45 ÷ 60 = 0.75, so the left-side time is 75% of the right.

title: Force was measured at three points during each landing. Which trial reached its highest force earliest?
options: All peaked at the same time
explanation: Trial A was highest at its first sample, 50 ms. A peak’s timing can differ even when peak values are similar.

title: A patient’s maximum walking distance improves, but they still avoid the stairs at home. Which outcome best reflects their original goal?
options: Whether they can climb their home stairs with acceptable symptoms
The therapist’s estimate of quadriceps size
explanation: A task relevant to the patient’s daily life directly measures progress toward their goal.

title: Why does holding the same dumbbell farther from the elbow make an isometric curl harder when the forearm stays horizontal?
explanation: External torque equals force multiplied by its perpendicular distance from the axis.

title: A runner has trouble lowering slowly from a heel raise. What kind of calf contraction controls the descent?
explanation: The calf produces tension while lengthening as the heel lowers.
hint: The muscle is active while getting longer.

title: An athlete moves from 2 sessions of 30 minutes to 3 sessions of 25 minutes in a week. What happens to weekly exercise time?
explanation: The original total is 60 minutes and the new total is 75 minutes.

title: Which plan increased weekly running time the most between Weeks 1 and 3?
explanation: Plan A rose from 40 to 65 minutes, a gain of 25 minutes. B gained 10 and C gained none.

title: In a movement screen, a runner’s knee drifts inward during a step-down. Which statement is best supported?
options: It proves a hip muscle is weak
It is an observed movement pattern worth exploring with more context
It predicts exactly when they will get injured
explanation: A single observation describes movement. It does not establish the cause or predict an injury on its own.

title: During walking with a single cane to unload a sore left hip, which hand typically holds the cane?
options: Either hand has the same mechanical effect
explanation: A cane in the opposite hand can help reduce the demand on the hip abductors during stance.
hint: Think about the opposite side from the sore hip.

title: A patient can lift more weight than last month, but their symptoms and daily activities have not changed. Which conclusion fits the data?
options: Strength improved in the tested task
The pain will definitely improve next week
They no longer need any support
explanation: The result supports improvement in the tested task. Other outcomes need their own measures.

title: Which rider shows the largest increase in heart rate from rest to minute 6?
explanation: B rose by 54 beats per minute, compared with 40 for A and 35 for C.

title: A bridge is held motionless at the top for 15 seconds. What best describes the action of the hip extensors during the hold?
explanation: They produce tension while the hip angle stays approximately constant.

title: A runner times the same 400 m route. Their average time changes from 100 seconds to 90. By what percentage did completion time decrease?
explanation: The reduction is 10 seconds divided by the original 100 seconds, or 10%.

title: Why does sitting down slowly generally require the quadriceps to work even though the knee is bending?
options: They are shortening to bend the knee
They are lengthening to control knee flexion
They pull the hip into extension
explanation: The quadriceps generate knee extension torque while lengthening to control the descent.
hint: Think of a brake on the way down.

title: A study reports that a test is highly sensitive for a particular condition. Which interpretation is most accurate?
options: Most people with the condition test positive
Most positive results prove the condition
Most people without it test negative
A positive result always identifies the cause
explanation: Sensitivity is the proportion of people with the condition who test positive.

title: An athlete rates symptoms right after exercise and later that day. Which session had the largest increase after the immediate check?
explanation: C rose from 2 to 6 between the immediate check and evening, the largest increase.

title: What’s the best way to make a repeated single-leg balance test comparable across visits?
options: Keep footwear, surface, instructions and timing consistent
Change the tested leg each time
explanation: Standardized test conditions reduce variation unrelated to actual change.

title: An athlete walks at 5 km/h for 12 minutes. How far do they cover?
explanation: Twelve minutes is one-fifth of an hour. At 5 km/h that is 1 km.

title: A runner says ‘ركبتي بتوجعني بس بالنزلة’. Which task is the closest clinic comparison to their complaint?
explanation: A step-down simulates lowering the body, a key demand when walking downhill.
hint: بالنزلة means on the way down.

title: A runner’s 6-minute walk improves from 420 m to 465 m. With your protocol, changes under 30 m can reflect measurement variability. The runner still avoids their target hill. What can you conclude?
options: They are definitely ready for the hill
The walk test suggests improved capacity, and hill tolerance still needs its own assessment
The walk test change is under 30 m
The walking data prove their pain is gone
explanation: The 45 m gain exceeds the stated variability threshold, but level walking and hill tolerance measure different tasks.
